title: NOX METALS vs McMaster-Carr for Aluminum Plate and Stock
summary: McMaster-Carr ships standard-size aluminum same or next day at a convenience premium. NOX METALS cuts plate to any size from certified mill stock. A straight comparison of when each one is the cheaper answer.
body_markdown:
### Is McMaster-Carr expensive for aluminum?


McMaster charges a convenience premium in exchange for same or next day delivery, enormous catalog breadth, and no sourcing effort. On a single prototype piece that trade is usually worth it. On repeat quantities or thick plate the premium compounds, and cut-to-size from a plate supplier is materially cheaper per finished part.


### Does McMaster-Carr cut aluminum to size?


McMaster is built around standard stock sizes rather than arbitrary cut-to-size plate work. If you need a specific rectangle out of a thick plate, that is a plate supplier job.


### Does McMaster-Carr sell 7050 aluminum?


Not that we have found. They stock 7075, which they describe as tight-tolerance extra-high-strength aluminum, along with 20-plus other aluminum alloys. For 7050-T7451 to AMS 4050 you need a plate supplier that stocks aerospace alloys.


### Does McMaster-Carr provide mill certs?


They offer material certificates for traceability. Whether that satisfies your requirement depends on the print: a DFARS flow-down asks specifically for melt source, which is a different document from a traceability certificate.


### What is buy-to-fly and why does it matter here?


Buy-to-fly is the ratio of material purchased to material remaining in the finished part. A catalog buy forces you up to the nearest standard size, so your ratio gets worse and you pay full price for metal you turn into chips. It is the single number that decides catalog versus cut-to-size, and our calculator will give it to you in about a minute.
